newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES SOAR 9.9 PCT ON FOREIGN BUYING.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES SOAR 9.9 PCT ON FOREIGN BUYING.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares soared 9.9 percent by the close on Thursday on a wave of liquidity from both foreign institutions and Hong Kong investors, brokers said.
B shares skyrocketed in the morning on the foreign buying and investors refused to sell in the afternoon, pointing to further rises on Friday, they said.

The B index closed 7.227 points higher, or a rise of 9.86 percent -- near the 10 percent daily limit-up -- to 80.496 points on strong turnover of $23.748 million, compared with $15.267 million on Wednesday.
"Liquidity from foreign investors has entered the market," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm in Shanghai. "H shares have been so good that B shares have taken their turn."
H shares, shares of Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong, have recently registered meteoric rises.
Rumours that China would allow the establishment of joint investment funds between foreign and Chinese institutions to trade in B shares also supported the rise, analysts said.
Such funds would give domestic investors investing in the funds an indirect means to buy foreign currency B shares, which are technically reserved for foreigners, they said.
"There was talk that foreign and domestic instutions could cooperate to set up funds to invest in B shares," said an analyst at a Japanese securities firm.
A Shanghai Stock Exchange official denied the rumour.

However, market watchdog the China Securities Regulatory Commission has recently hinted it would like to promote investment funds and joint venture mutual funds in China in the second half, analysts said.
Of Shanghai's 47 B shares, all gained on Thursday with most hitting their daily limit up of 10 percent.
Building machinery maker Shanghai Jintai Co was the top B share gainer, roaring ahead $0.012 or 10.17 percent to $0.130.
Recently listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co was the most actively traded B share on institutional buying. It surged $0.042 or 9.68 percent to $0.476 on volume of around 6.1 million shares.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares benefitted from the sharp gains in the B index but trading was not as active, brokers said.
The A index closed up 48.325 points or 4.13 percent to 1,218.933 on turnover of 3.402 billion yuan against 3.083 billion on Wednesday.
The SSE30 blue chip rose 163.878 points or 4.68 percent to 3,665.727 points.
Brokers said both the A and B share markets had further room to gain in the short term with the B index likely to rise sharply on Friday.
"Some (B share) firms will report poor results in the coming days, but it will not change the rising trend amid bullish market sentiment," one local broker said.
